Sub: Levy of Damages U/S 14 B - Discretion to vary rates of damages — reg.

Ref: Your Letter No. 14068/EPF/SRO/GKP/Legal dated 07-04-2015

Sir,

Please refer to your letter cited above. The matter has been examined and the
views of Head Officé are provided below.

2. | It can be seen that the Section 14B of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 provides that the
Commissioner may recover frorn the employer by way of penalty such damages not
exceeding the amount of arrears, as may be specified in the Scheme. Since the Act
clearly specifies that the levy of damages shall be as specified in the Scheme, the rates
specified under the EPF Scheme 1952 under Para 32A shall be adopted without any
deviation. It is therefore clear that the Act does not provide any discretion on the Inquiry
Authority for varying the rates of Damages to be recovered from the defaulting employer.
The EPF Scheme 1952, under Para 32B, separately provides for reduction / waiver of
damages levied as per which the Central Board, EPF is empowered for the purpose.
Therefore the Employer aggrieved by the order of levy of Penal Damages has to
approach the Central Board of EPF for reduction / waiver of the same. The CBT will then

consider the case on merits separately subject to the provisibns of the EPF & MP Act
1952 and the Schemes framed thereunder.

3. It can be seen that the Authority levying Penal Damages under Section 14B of the
EPF & MP Act, 1952 shall provide an opportunity of hearing to the party concerned for
meeting the requirements of the law of principles of natural justice. The requirements of
the principles of law of natural justice is that all the parties conéérned shall be provided
with an opportunity to present their case before a decislon against their interest is taken.

In the! case of levy of penal damages, issues to be considered are, whether there is a
delay in remittance, whether the delay stated in the notice is correct, whether the delay
is due'to,some situation beyond the control of the employer like disruption to normalcy of
public life due to disturbance like natural calamities, strike, bandh, etc. In such cases
where the delay is @% due to situation stated above, the authority can consider and revise
the amount / date. -

4, Since there are two different authorities specified for two different purposes under
the law ie. for levy of damages and for reduction / waiver of damages, the authorities
cannot interfere with one another's powers for the sake of regularity in the action

5. It is therefore opined that the above may be placed before the Court for
consideration and the court can be informed that since the power to reduce or waive
damages is available at a different level the employers aggrieved by the PD Order can
approach such competent authority for consideration after the damages are levied by
inquiry:authority and there is no need for inquiry authority to exercise the same power.

This issues with approval of ACC (Compliance).
